extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, IP practitioners, researchers and general readers seeking information about the Eurasian Patent Organization
extracted.subtask_description: A factual overview of the Eurasian Patent Organization (EAPO): its mandate under the Eurasian Patent Convention, membership/withdrawal rules, international cooperation (PPH, documentation exchange), and its status under the PCT as an ISA/IPEA. Useful for understanding procedural/organizational aspects affecting patent filing and prosecution in the Eurasian region.

rubrics_metrics.name: EAPO mandate under the Eurasian Patent Convention
rubrics_metrics.description: The Eurasian Patent Organization (EAPO) is an international organization set up in 1995 by the Eurasian Patent Convention (EAPC) to grant Eurasian patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes that the EAPO's core function is to grant Eurasian patents under the framework of the EAPC. The article identifies the EAPO as the regional patent-granting authority for contracting states; no further procedural details of patentability or examination are given on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official language requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The official language of the EAPO is Russian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication for filings and proceedings: Russian is the EAPO's working language (relevant for submissions, communications, translations and interpretation of documents). The article does not provide filing-language rules but flags Russian as the office language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership rule (Article 2(2) EAPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 2(2) EAPC (English translation): 'All Contracting States shall be members of the Organization.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines membership as tied to being a Contracting State to the Eurasian Patent Convention. The page lists current contracting/member states (Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Russia) and notes original signatories that have not ratified (e.g., Ukraine, Georgia).

rubrics_metrics.name: Denunciation / withdrawal procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: A Contracting State may denounce the Eurasian Patent Convention; denunciation leads to the state ceasing to be a party after the applicable notice/effective period (example: Moldova denounced the Convention on 26 October 2011 and ceased to be party on 26 April 2012).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows that membership can be terminated by denunciation with an effective date; the page uses Moldova as an example and notes subsequent cooperation by Moldova (cooperation agreement with EAPO, validation agreement with EPO). Exact notice periods and legal effects are not detailed on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation and cooperation agreements as alternative coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Validation and cooperation agreements (e.g., between the EPO and a national office) can provide patent coverage or cooperation even where a state is not a member of the EAPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example given: a validation agreement between the European Patent Office and Moldova took effect on 1 November 2015, allowing European patents to cover Moldova despite Moldova's withdrawal from the EAPC. The page indicates such agreements are options for extending patent coverage or cooperation outside formal EAPC membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation in the Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) Programme
rubrics_metrics.description: The PPH Programme constitutes bilateral agreements between the Eurasian Patent Office and other patent offices designed to provide applicants with opportunities to get a patent faster and more efficiently in participating offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation allows accelerated examination of patents compared to applications from non-participating patent offices. The article lists partner offices participating with EAPO (Japan Patent Office, European Patent Office, China National Intellectual Property Administration, Korean Intellectual Property Office, and the Finnish Patent and Registration Office). Useful when planning parallel filings or seeking expedited prosecution using positive work products from partner offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchange of patent documentation agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: The EAPO maintains various agreements on the exchange of patent documentation with 38 countries across Asia, Europe, and North America.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitates access to prior art and cooperation on patent information. The page states this as part of EAPO's international cooperation activities but does not list the specific countries or the terms of exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition as International Searching Authority (ISA) and International Preliminary Examining Authority (IPEA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The EAPO is recognized as an International Searching Authority and an International Preliminary Examining Authority under the PCT system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables EAPO to act as ISA/IPEA for international (PCT) applications, performing international searches and preliminary examinations. The page notes this status but does not provide procedural details (scope, languages accepted, fees, or national limitations).
